_about: Manifest of ODBC drivers under stress-test. Single source of truth for (a) the version of each driver to install in CI, (b) the URL/apt package to install it from, and (c) the upstream git repo + tag whose source matches that binary version. Consumed by .github/workflows/stress-test.yml at runtime via `jq` and by the /triage-driver skill at analysis time. apt_version strings are formatted for `apt-get install pkg=version`; if Ubuntu drops a pinned version from its repos the workflow will fail loudly at the install step and this file must be updated. The `version` field is the upstream form (what SQLGetInfo reports); apt_version is the Debian-formatted form. Firebird is included as of v3.5.0-rc1 (the first release of the refactored driver). H11 adds a `provenance` block per driver, read only by the triage skill: it declares whether actual_version.txt is a real observation or an echo of this file, and whether SQLGetInfo(SQL_DRIVER_VER) can be trusted. Without it the skill's version cross-check compared the manifest against itself for three drivers and could not fail. Purely additive - the workflow does not read it.

provenance._note: actual_version.txt carries `dpkg -s odbc-postgresql | awk '/^Version:/'`, which is a genuine observation of what got installed. Debian form (epoch `1:`, revision `-1`) differs from the upstream `version` field; the triage comparer normalises both before matching.
Same as postgresql: actual_version.txt comes from `dpkg -s odbc-mariadb`, and the job fails loudly if it disagrees with apt_version.

actual_version.txt is parsed out of the extracted `mysql-connector-odbc-<version>-linux-*` directory name, so it reflects the tarball that was actually unpacked rather than the URL that was requested.

H11. Both halves of the provenance cross-check are unusable for this driver, and saying so is the point of this block. (a) The job has no version string to extract from the bare .so, so it echoes this file's `version` into actual_version.txt - comparing the two therefore compares the manifest with itself and can never fail. (b) DuckDB answers SQLGetInfo(SQL_DRIVER_VER) with `03.51.0000`, its ODBC *compliance level*, not its product version, so driver_info.driver_version is no help either. Triage reports this as PROVENANCE=UNVERIFIABLE rather than a false OK. Use SQL_DBMS_VER if you need a real number at runtime.

install._note: Server brought up via ClickHouse's own deb repo; server version is not part of the triage contract — only the driver version is pinned.

provenance._note: H11. The job echoes this file's `version` into actual_version.txt, so that comparison is the manifest against itself. driver_info.driver_version is believed usable here (unlike duckdb/firebird), so triage falls back to it as the one genuinely observed value.

install._note: Server brought up via PSFirebird (Firebird 5.0.3); the .tar.gz ships only libOdbcFb.so + odbcinst.ini.sample, registered manually.

provenance._note: H11. Same shape as duckdb, found the same way - by reading a stored artifact. The .tar.gz carries no extractable version, so actual_version.txt is an echo of this file's `version`; and the driver answers SQLGetInfo(SQL_DRIVER_VER) with `00.00.000`, which is why the old skill's cross-check passed a driver that reported no version at all. PROVENANCE=UNVERIFIABLE is the honest answer until the driver reports a real version or CI observes one.

install._note: F8: this said method 'release_asset' with a releases/latest URL, while stress-test.yml has always downloaded the artifact from the most recent successful master ci.yml run - so the manifest sent readers to a route nothing takes, which matters because this file is the source of truth the /triage-driver skill reads. Using CI is deliberate: it closes the release-cadence gap, so a stress-test run exercises the driver as it is now rather than as it was at the last tag. Mock driver is built from this repo; for triage the 'source' is the workspace itself, not a remote clone.
install._release_asset_note: What a *user* installs, and it does exist - kept for that reason, not used by CI. release.yml publishes this for Windows only, though ci.yml now builds the mock on all three platforms.

source._note: Triage skill special-cases mock-driver — no clone step, points at this repo's mock-driver/ directory directly.

provenance._note: H11. `version` is the literal string "workspace"; actual_version.txt carries the 12-char short SHA of the master CI run the binary came from. There is no version to cross-check, so triage skips the comparison and records the SHA as the workspace state to diff against.
